thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER — HIGH severity — WAF alert: credential stuffing pattern detected against /v1/session and /v1/auth endpoints. Spike from ~20k -> 120k req/min, many 401s. Mitigation suggested: temporary WAF IP block + tighten per-key rate limits. Logs: https://logs.redwood.example/alerts/1718205472 :rotating_light:

maria: I'm on it, paging SRE and eng-runtime. Confirmed spike in the last 3m. Traffic profile shows distinct user-agent bot patterns and repeated login attempts per account.

ashwin: copying runbook now: https://runbooks.redwood.example/credential-stuffing. First actions: 1) apply WAF block for offending ASNs/IP ranges 2) throttle anonymous endpoints 3) increase auth endpoint strictness (fail2ban-like behaviour).

lee: Can we do a quick per-customer impact check? Any enterprise customers affected?

maria: Early look: mobile app auths failing ~12% for some high-volume tenants (mainly older API keys). No evidence of data exfiltration. SLO alerts firing for latency on /v1/auth.

priya: I'll open a CS ticket for top 5 tenants we think are impacted and patch the status page. support-jane can help notify.

support-jane: ok prepping messages. Do we have ETA for mitigation?

maria: Working on mitigation now. Applying WAF block to top offending CIDR blocks. Running command: 

```
# add temporary blocklist rule
POST /waf/rules HTTP/1.1
Host: waf-api.internal
Authorization: Bearer $WAF_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{ "rule_name": "tmp-cred-stuffing-1718205472", "action": "block", "conditions": { "ip_cidr": ["203.0.113.0/24","198.51.100.0/24"], "ua_regex": "(python-requests|curl|bot)" }, "ttl_minutes": 60 }
```

Applied rule, response 200. :thumbsup:

ashwin: After block, enable per-key rate limit change on auth endpoints for unverified keys to 10r/min. Command to patch limiter: 

```
PATCH /config/ratelimit HTTP/1.1
Host: control-plane.internal
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN
Content-Type: application/json

{ "route": "/v1/auth", "scope": "api_key_unverified", "limit_per_min": 10 }
```

I've pushed the change to prod config. Rolling out via canary to region eu-west-1 first.

lee: Any risk to high-tier enterprise keys? We should whitelist dedicated keys.

maria: Good point — we are applying scope to unverified / default keys only. Dedicated and enterprise tiers are excluded by tag:tier=enterprise.

jordan: Noted abnormal traffic coming from cloud provider X ASN 12345; added ASN to WAF block and set block TTL 120m. Also activated heavier CAPTCHA on auth web flows behind the CDN.

priya: Status page updated: "Investigating authentication errors and elevated error rate for auth endpoints. Mitigation in progress."

support-jane: Notified top 5 customers via email + slack. CS asked for any workaround — recommended token rotation for impacted keys, and to switch to enterprise keys if persistent.

maria: Quick customer impact summary for incident channel: ~3% of overall auths failed globally; certain tenants saw up to 12% auth failures. No data loss. Primary mitigation: WAF CIDR blocks & per-key rate limit change.

ashwin: Monitoring metrics: auth 5xx down from 18% -> 6% within 4m of mitigation. Request rate for offending UA dropped 90%.

lee: Great. Can we also throttle embedding/search endpoints that are being scraped? Those are a secondary target.

maria: Yup, applying temporary quota: embeddings route -> 5k req/min global burst 1k, per-key hard quota 500 req/min. Patching now.

jordan: Added IP challenge rule on CDN for suspicious UA > 50 r/min: return 403 + CAPTCHA header.

priya: Handoff to night on-call in 30m: ashwin will take over monitoring and coordinate any ramp-down or rollback.

ashwin: I have the baton. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and ensure support notifications are updated. Plan: maintain blocks for 2 hours, then gradually relax if no recurrence, run postmortem.

maria: Filing incident INC-2024-459 and linking this thread. Adding initial impact notes and timeline.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-459 (severity: S2) — owner: maria — runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.example/credential-stuffing — pager acknowledged.

support-jane: CS flagged one enterprise complaining about increased latency due to CDN challenge; sending note to them.

ashwin: Quick log excerpts showing repeated auth attempts: 
```
2024-07-12T11:12:01Z 198.51.100.45 POST /v1/auth 401 ua="python-requests/2.28" acc_id="user123" attempts=45
2024-07-12T11:13:04Z 203.0.113.9 POST /v1/auth 401 ua="curl/7.68.0" acc_id="user234" attempts=120
```

maria: We'll keep this thread until we close. Next steps: 1) Ashwin monitor for 60m, 2) remove temporary CIDR blocks after safe window, 3) schedule postmortem and add mitigations to runbook (adaptive per-key scoring, CAPTCHA escalations).

ashwin: Acknowledged. Current status: mitigations in place, auth error rate falling, customer notifications sent. Setting reminder for 60m to reassess then update incident. :white_check_mark:
